newsitem.title: USA: Dole uses last radio address to attack Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Dole uses last radio address to attack Clinton.

text.p: Republican challenger Bob Dole delivered his last weekly radio address on Saturday before Tuesday's election, taking swipes at President Bill Clinton and spelling out his own beliefs.

In a five-minute address taped during a bus trip through Michigan late on Friday, Dole said he wanted to cut taxes, but "President Clinton disagrees." He said he wanted to balance the budget, but Clinton had vetoed two balanced budgets sent to him by the Republican Congress.
He also said parents should have the opportunity to send children to any school they wanted, but Clinton had opposed Dole's plan for vouchers.

Dole said he would like to lead a renewed fight against drug use, but Clinton has "turned his back on this critical issue." He also hoped to strengthen and save Medicare, Dole said, accusing Clinton of playing political games with Medicare and frightening seniors over the health care programme.
Dole said he wants a militarily strong nation, but "President Clinton has recklessly cut our defences, ignoring the threats of a dangerous world."
"I want a White House that never compromises its ethics or violates its word," Dole said of questionable campaign contributions.
"I believe in the honour of that office -- the highest in this land, the highest in this world -- and I am still offended when that honour is betrayed," Dole said.
Dole, who is on a non-stop campaign tour until the election, said: "I wish I could shake the hands of every one of you. And I am going to do my very best."
He closed the broadcast by saying that if he did meet listeners face to face, they should "look carefully at the men who seek your vote. Cast a vote you will always be proud of."
